questions.question_text: According to the chapter, why are rehearsal techniques important for high school students preparing for a speech?

options.text: They allow students to avoid practicing altogether
They help improve fluency, confidence, and delivery through structured practice, ensuring a smoother performance
They focus only on memorizing lines without considering delivery
They are unnecessary if a student is naturally confidentCorrect Answer:B. They help improve fluency, confidence, and delivery through structured practice, ensuring a smoother performance

questions.question_text: What does the chapter suggest as a key benefit of recording and self-review when polishing speech delivery?

options.text: It allows students to avoid feedback from others
It provides an outside perspective to spot strengths and areas for improvement, like filler words or gestures
It is only useful for professional speakers, not students
It discourages students by focusing only on flawsCorrect Answer:B. It provides an outside perspective to spot strengths and areas for improvement, like filler words or gestures

questions.question_text: How does the chapter recommend structuring peer feedback sessions to make them effective?

options.text: By only giving negative feedback to highlight mistakes
By using a feedback sandwich—starting with a positive, suggesting a fix, and ending with praise—to balance encouragement and improvement
By avoiding specific suggestions to keep things vague

By refusing to accept feedback to maintain confidenceCorrect Answer:B. By using a feedback sandwich—starting with a positive, suggesting a fix, and ending with praise—to balance encouragement and improvement

questions.question_text: What is a primary focus of time management in speech delivery, as discussed in the chapter?

options.text: Speaking as quickly as possible to finish early
Staying within time limits by pacing content and editing for efficiency, ensuring key points are covered without rushing or dragging
Ignoring time limits to include all possible details

Adding extra stories to fill time even if irrelevantCorrect Answer:B. Staying within time limits by pacing content and editing for efficiency, ensuring key points are covered without rushing or dragging

questions.question_text: What is a common challenge teens face with peer feedback sessions, according to the chapter?

options.text: Always receiving perfect feedback without effort
Feeling fear of criticism or taking feedback personally, which can hinder participation or growth
Never having peers available to practice with
Finding feedback sessions too easy to organize and useCorrect Answer:B. Feeling fear of criticism or taking feedback personally, which can hinder participation or growth
